title: Replicating Correlated Errors on a Safety Benchmark Instead of a Leaderboard

original_idea.body:
# Replicating Correlated Errors on a Safety Benchmark Instead of a Leaderboard

**Problem:** Kim et al. measured error correlation on general leaderboards and hiring. Whether it holds for safety classification is untested - yet correlated safety misjudgments are far more dangerous.

**Direction:** Replicate the error-correlation methodology on a safety-classification task: have 6-10 open models classify labeled harmful/benign prompts and compute pairwise error-correlation. Twist: stratify by same-provider vs cross-provider and by model size.

**Why it matters:** Correlated safety misclassification means an ensemble of moderation models gives a false sense of robustness.

**Relevant context:** Direct replication of Correlated Errors in LLMs (arXiv:2506.07962) with a safety twist.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (correlated safety misclassification -> false moderation robustness) but a replication with a domain twist; impact incremental.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Binary classification with a published metric and public dataset; very tractable, no training.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped replication with clear stratified metrics and success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models/public data; correlated-failure measurement labs have little incentive to publish.

novelty.reasoning: Direct method replication with a safety twist; partly novel domain.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Method published; safety-classification domain application is the open slice.
